Must specify the database host and port explicitly, and if a connection is already open, call disconnect before reconnecting, since opening a second connection replaces the active session without closing the previous one.
Pass the package name or keyword only; scoped packages should include the @scope/name form so results match the registry's own search semantics rather than a partial substring guess.

Generate at most one active link per offer_id; requesting a new link before the previous one expires returns the same link rather than issuing a duplicate, so cache the result instead of calling this repeatedly.
Call with no argument or alias index first to see the list of valid aliases; passing an alias that does not exist returns an error instead of a fuzzy match.

Run this before create_chapter_draft or apply_dialogue_action_beats whenever a scene touches an existing character, item, or faction, so continuity references get updated rather than contradicted.

The dryRun parameter defaults to true and should stay true until the proposed labels and actions have been reviewed by a human; only set it to false once the classification is meant to be applied automatically.
ALWAYS run with dryRun set to true first and review the proposed links before applying changes across the whole vault, since this rewrites note content in place with no built-in undo.
Call list_connections first to confirm which connections are actually in a failed state; retrying a connection that is already open has no effect and simply returns its current status.

Confidence should reflect a measured success rate rather than a guess; store a pattern only after it has been observed to work at least once, since low-confidence entries are deprioritized when the bank ranks retrievals.

Only pass an invoice_id that has already been paid through the deeplink from xrpl_telemetry_get_quote; calling this with an unpaid or unknown invoice_id returns a pending status rather than telemetry data.
Must match an icon's canonical slug exactly as returned by list_icons or search_icons, including its numeric suffix such as home-01; a display name or partial match will not resolve to a glyph.

Keep duration short for interactive checks; anything past about 10 seconds switches to 500ms frames and produces a coarser screencast, so prefer take_screenshot instead when only a single moment matters.
Prefer the owner/repo short form over a full URL when known, since it resolves faster; keep maxDepth at 0 for a single page and only raise it to 1 when the whole wiki is needed.

Omit this to scope analytics to the current project; only pass all when a cross-project rollup is actually needed, since that comparison costs more to compute and mixes unrelated projects' memory stats together.

Name must be unique among open connections, since connecting again with a name already in use replaces the existing connection silently, and dialect must match the database engine or every subsequent query_read and query_write call against it will fail.

Write content as a standalone statement that makes sense without the current conversation, since memory_recall retrieves entries individually; a vague fragment is far less useful later than a specific decision or pattern.

Call this before get_reusable_component to confirm a component name and its supported variants exist, since requesting an unlisted component or unsupported size returns an error instead of a partial match.
Run this before modifying a function with more than a couple of call sites, and prefer direction both for a first pass so callers and callees show together instead of two separate calls.

Only include URLs that were actually returned in a previous tool response; do not construct or guess a documentation URL yourself, since unlisted paths on the source site are not guaranteed to exist or stay stable.
Schema defaults to dbo and should be set explicitly for any non-default schema, since two tables with the same tableName in different schemas will otherwise resolve to the wrong one.

Run this before ingest_file when unsure whether a document is already indexed, since re-ingesting a file already in the vector database creates a duplicate entry rather than updating the existing one.

Version may be omitted to refresh the latest indexed version, but must otherwise match a version already returned by find_version exactly; an approximate or unindexed version string re-scrapes nothing and returns an empty result.

The walletAddress parameter must be the wallet whose on-chain M32 balance is being checked, not an arbitrary address; a wallet holding fewer than 2,500,000 M32 receives a 403 rather than a partial comparison.

Sends immediately with no preview step, so verify channelId and message content beforehand; if sent in error, remove it with discord_delete_message rather than sending a correction message on top of it.

Reaction must match the emoji name already present on the message exactly, without colons; calling this when the named reaction is not present on the message returns an error rather than silently doing nothing.
Returns aggregate figures across all bookings visible to the current account; use warp_list_bookings when the underlying per-shipment records are needed rather than a summary total.
Prefer fetch_markdown or fetch_txt when you only need the readable content, since raw HTML from a heavy page can be large and slower to parse than the already-cleaned alternatives.
Always call with action get to review a listing's full details before action install, since installing adds the listing's tools to the target workspace immediately with no confirmation prompt.

Should match the component's exact exported name as it appears in Chakra UI, such as Button rather than a lowercase or pluralized variant; check list_components first when the exact spelling is not already known.
Call this only after a dev server is actually listening on the target port, since pointing the preview at a port with nothing bound to it just shows a connection error.
Offset moves forward in fixed pages of up to 20 results each rather than by individual result, so raise count before raising offset when only a few more results are needed.
Units must match one of the tool's supported area units exactly, such as hectares rather than ha; an abbreviated or unrecognized unit falls back to square meters rather than raising an error.
Model must already be pulled locally before calling this; run pull first if unsure, since requesting a model that is not present fails the call instead of downloading it automatically.
All statements run in a single transaction and are rolled back together if any one of them fails, so do not mix statements meant to succeed independently in the same call.

Provide company_number instead of company_name whenever it is already known, since name-based resolution can match the wrong company when multiple UK-registered businesses share a similar trading name.
Must be an absolute path to an existing Railway project workspace on disk; a path that has not been initialized with create-project-and-link first will cause the link to fail.
The instancePath must point to an existing Model or Folder in the current place, not a single Part, since exporting a loose part produces a build file with no meaningful palette or bounding box.
The id must be the document's original identifier rather than a title or slug; if unsure which id to use, look it up first via get-v1-documents or get-v2-documents depending on the target version.
The projectId, once set, cannot be changed later and must be globally unique across all of GCP, so leave it unset to auto-generate one rather than guessing a short name that likely already exists.
Use browser_click for pointer interactions instead of simulating Tab and Enter sequences here, since key presses are dispatched to whatever element currently has focus rather than a specific target.
Image must be reachable as a URL, a data URI, or a local path under 5 MB; a source image over that limit or in an unsupported format is rejected rather than automatically downscaled.
Should be an id already returned by list_accounts for a Pinterest account specifically; passing an id belonging to a different connected platform returns an empty board list rather than an error.
The attachmentId is only valid within the thread it was listed under; fetch it via get_thread first if the id is not already on hand, since ids are not guaranteed unique across threads.

Name performs a fuzzy match, so avoid regex or wildcard characters entirely since they are matched literally rather than as patterns, and narrow with kind when a common name matches definitions of more than one type.

Call action check before relying on detect_godot's result in a fresh environment, and call action status after any set to confirm the new value actually took effect rather than assuming the write succeeded.

Call this before arxiv_search whenever the exact category code is not already known, since arxiv_search matches category filters literally and an invalid or misspelled code silently returns zero results instead of an error.
Navigating away from the current page discards any unsaved state in forms or scripts on that page, so complete or capture what is needed with browser_evaluate before calling this.

The uid must reference an actual file input or an element that opens a native file chooser on the current page snapshot; an outdated uid from a previous snapshot taken before the page changed will fail.
Limit and offset paginate independently of period and interval, so raise offset rather than period when older bars are needed within the same interval, and keep limit at or below 100 per call.

Run this once after connecting a new repository and whenever searchFiles or searchIssues starts returning unexpectedly empty results, since a repository over GitHub's indexing size limit degrades search silently rather than raising an error.

Raise timeout above the 10-second default for pages with slow initial script execution; a value of 0 does not disable the timeout, it simply falls back to the default rather than waiting indefinitely.
Must be the asset's exact ticker as used across the rest of this API, matching what skew_get_spot and skew_get_iv_smile accept, not a display name or trading-pair string with a slash.

Set include_full_text to false and use per-source pages instead whenever a source is more than a few dozen pages, since returning full text for a large PDF inflates the response far more than a targeted page range.

Calling with action get requires a slug obtained from a prior action list call in the same namespace; guessing a slug from a page title rarely matches, since slugs are URL-encoded and can differ from the display title.

Checking a context handle's stats never consumes or expires it, unlike sverklo_ctx_peek or sverklo_ctx_slice, so call this first whenever you only need to confirm a handle is still fresh before spending it.
The key must be unique within the organization and should be treated as permanent once set; start a fresh tag instead of reusing a retired key for an unrelated purpose later on.

Omitting wiki logs out of every connected wiki at once, not just the current one, so pass wiki explicitly when only a single connection should be revoked; check oauth-status first if unsure which wikis are currently authenticated.

The queryParams.status field filters to one or more job states at once; when scanning for stuck jobs, pair scheduled_before with a recent timestamp rather than paging through the entire unfiltered list with count and offset alone.

The safeSearch parameter defaults to whatever the server is configured with rather than moderate, so set it explicitly when a query's results must be reproducible across environments, and keep query under the 400-character limit.
Kept only as a fallback for single-sender workflows; once a session uses more than one sender, set lastSenderIds instead, since lastSenderId alone cannot represent a multi-sender session on its own.

The job_id must reference a job already started by the find-people-at-companies workflow; calling this before that job exists produces an empty CSV rather than an error, so confirm rows are present before feeding the file to growth_upload_csv_to_sequence.

Set includeTimestamp only when the block time is actually needed, since it costs an extra RPC call, and pass network as either a chain's common name or its numeric chain ID consistently across related calls.
Call this once to resolve a station code before calling get_air_quality, since that tool expects an exact station code rather than a canton name or free-text location.

Leave empty to list all income types on the first page rather than guessing a search term; keep limit at or below the recommended 13 and follow next_token for subsequent pages instead of increasing limit further.
Term should be the exact word or short phrase being looked up, not a full question; for terms with more than one meaning on Hacker News, the most common current usage is returned first.

Set security_score above zero to exclude newly-deployed or unverified contracts from the results, since unfiltered top-gainer lists are frequently dominated by illiquid tokens with negligible trading history.

Must be an absolute filesystem path to the workbook rather than a bare filename; a relative path resolves against whatever directory the process happens to be running in and will fail unpredictably on shared or scheduled runs.
Obtain webhookId from createWebhook or a prior listing before calling this; a webhookId that was never issued or has since been deleted returns a not-found error rather than an empty record.

Verify the target node and method name with get_td_node_errors or get_td_class_details beforehand, since invoking an unsupported method on a live node can leave its internal state inconsistent until the project is reloaded.

Every call re-runs the full compliance suite against url — do NOT poll this in a loop waiting for a grade to change. Use mcp_compliance_explain instead when only interpreting a grade you already have.
Read get_overview first if the project's current Taiga UI version is not already known, because the returned migration steps assume you can already identify your starting version.
Point this at a workbook that already exists on disk and is closed in Excel; writing formulas to a file that is currently open elsewhere can silently fail or corrupt the workbook.
Provide the project's absolute root directory rather than a single subfolder or file; scoping this to part of the project silently omits the rest from the scan and inflates the resulting score.
Confirm topic identifiers against list-topics before calling this, since a topics value that list-topics never returned narrows the search to zero documents instead of raising an error.

Pass a bare domain such as example.invalid, with no scheme or path segments; guidance is cached per exact domain string, so a subdomain should be queried on its own if its selectors might differ from the parent site's.
Must match one of this tool's defined operation names exactly, such as the team-list or single-team lookup; an unrecognized value is rejected outright rather than falling back to the broadest read.
Set an explicit limit and page through results for large design systems, since an unbounded call can return several thousand entries, and turning on includeVariants multiplies that further.

Each entry's name must match an existing shared label exactly, including case; check current names with todoist_get_shared_labels beforehand, because an entry naming a label that does not exist is silently skipped rather than reported as an error.

Select source runtime only while the game is actively playing, since it reads live connections from the running SceneTree and errors out against a stopped game rather than falling back to the saved scene file.
Choose outputType svg or mermaid when the diagram will need further edits, because base64 and the url variants render a one-way image that cannot be reopened for editing afterward.
A dump runs synchronously and can take a long time against a large database. NEVER trigger this repeatedly during peak load, and confirm outputFile will not overwrite a backup still needed.
Include the scheme (https:// or http://) at the start of the address; a bare hostname or path without one will fail to load rather than silently defaulting to https.
Request readHeadings first on long pages to locate the right section before pulling full content, since repeated calls with a large maxLength mostly return boilerplate navigation and footer text.

Must reference a project where the target function is already deployed; pairing a valid project_id with a function name that does not exist in it returns a not-found response rather than deploying anything.
Supply either config or an explicit input spec path; when neither one resolves to a real file, generation fails outright instead of searching parent directories for a fallback.
Look this up before search_overpass whenever the exact tag spelling for a category is uncertain, since a query built on a guessed tag name returns zero results rather than an error.

Omitting selector captures the full viewport at the given width and height; supplying a selector instead captures only that element, which is the more reliable choice for content sitting below the fold.

This MUST be called once at the start of a session, before any other project tool; calling it again mid-session re-fetches the same cold-start snapshot and will not reflect anything written with remember since then.

Requires dkg_assertion_create to have already been run for the named assertion. IMPORTANT: promotion makes the content visible to every teammate with shared-graph access, so omit entities only when the whole assertion should be published.

Enable recursive before scanning a new directory tree, since a non-recursive pass only inspects top-level files and will miss anything nested in subdirectories; request format json when the output feeds into another automated step.
Closes the active tab immediately with NO confirmation prompt and no way to recover unsaved input on that page — save or submit any in-progress work first.

filename should carry the correct extension, since downstream viewers infer content type from it rather than from the file bytes, and file must be the complete contents encoded as base64 with no line breaks.
Navigating away from the current page invalidates every element reference returned by an earlier snapshot; take a fresh snapshot before the next click_by_uid or fill_by_uid call.

Prefer this over checking pricing or risk in isolation when a service has not yet been chosen, since it cross-references both together; state real values for budget and region, as vague ones return an overly broad candidate list.
Run this before create_repository to check whether a project with the intended name already exists, since creating one with a duplicate name is permitted and will not raise a warning.

Coordinates must be decimal degrees, positive for north and east and negative for south and west, never degrees-minutes-seconds; batch every point into one locations array rather than issuing a separate call per point.
Phrase query as a specific concept or component name rather than a full sentence; broad phrasing returns many loosely related sections and makes the exact page harder to find.
Must uniquely identify a single element; a selector matching several elements only evaluates the first one found and can pass even while other matches on the page remain visible.

max_results caps at one thousand per call regardless of a larger requested value; when the response carries a next_page_token, pass it back through page_token rather than treating the first page as the complete listing.
Omit on the first call to retrieve the index of valid paths; a path not present in that index returns a not-found error instead of a fuzzy match against the nearest resource.
Works best as a single broad term, such as a sector name, rather than a full question; combining several concepts into one keyword tends to return no matches at all instead of a ranked list.
Narrow with tags or name before pulling detail on individual monitors through get_monitor_details, since an unfiltered listing on a large account can return several hundred monitors in one response.

An SSH-style address needs a key already loaded in the calling environment's SSH agent; without one configured, use an HTTPS address instead so a failure surfaces as a clear error rather than a silent hang.
Terminates the ENTIRE browser process, not just the active tab: unsaved state in every other open tab is lost, and every other puppeteer_* call fails until a new instance is launched.
Returns milliseconds since epoch in UTC, not local time; convert explicitly before comparing against a timestamp expressed in a specific time zone.
Set to custom only when startDate is also supplied in year-month-day form; leaving startDate empty while this is custom raises an error instead of quietly defaulting to today.

Raise this above the default whenever the person completing the browser authorization step may need more than five minutes, since the call fails once the timeout elapses even if the browser window is still open waiting for input.
Must be the block's identifier exactly as returned by API-get-block-children, hyphens included; passing a page identifier here instead returns a bad request rather than that page's top-level block.

Identifies the specific linter or analyzer that reported the pattern, not the project or repository being analyzed; look it up with codacy_list_tools first if only the pattern's display name is known.

Reports cumulative spend against spend_limit for the single delegation_id given, so query each delegation separately when an agent holds more than one; totals are never aggregated across delegations in one call.

Check this before any other tool in the same family at the start of a session to confirm credentials are already configured; when status comes back unauthenticated, follow spotify_setup_instructions rather than guessing at the required fields.
ALWAYS run this before vl_bulk_delete_saved_objects on anything that may be referenced elsewhere — deletion itself is irreversible and does not check for dependent dashboards on its own.

Set distance well past the refresh-trigger threshold of the target screen, since a short pull reads as an ordinary scroll and will not trigger a refresh; leave locate unset to pull from the current viewport center.

Keep this a short, self-contained snippet in the language the rule targets; it is parsed in isolation, so code depending on imports or context from other files can fail to parse even when the rule itself is correct.

Omit category to list every token type in one call; requesting a category name that does not exist in this design system returns an empty list rather than the full set, so check spelling before narrowing.

Leave unset on a first call to see the whole catalog before narrowing; pairing an unset category with verbose returns a large enough response to noticeably slow things down, so combine them only once a category is known.
conversation_id must reference a conversation that has already ended; feedback submitted while a conversation is still active is rejected outright rather than queued for delivery once it closes.

Check valid names with list_categories beforehand; an unrecognized category in the array is skipped silently rather than raising an error, so confirm the resulting tool list instead of assuming every requested category activated.

Must be the root address to map, scheme included; pair this with select_domains whenever the site spans multiple subdomains, since without it the crawler can wander onto unrelated linked domains and exhaust limit before finishing the intended site.

Point this at the directory holding the project's package.json and ui5.yaml, not a subfolder such as the app source directory; pointing elsewhere misdetects the framework version and returns API results for the wrong release.

Use the exact component or hook name as listed by list_items, case-sensitive; a near-miss spelling returns no documentation at all, so search_docs is the better choice when the precise name is not already known.
Set resource_type to match what number actually identifies; giving the wrong resource_type for that number posts the comment to the wrong timeline instead of returning a not-found error.
Deletion is immediate and this tool offers NO undo. Confirm the id is the intended element with query_elements first, especially on a canvas where group_elements has been used.
Accepts only the status-check keyword this tool defines; any other value is rejected, since checking sign-in state is all this tool does and it does not itself perform sign-in or sign-out.
ToRecipients needs at least one entry with a valid emailAddress.address. IMPORTANT: this only creates a draft and never sends it — a separate send step is still required once reviewed.

Set model_ceiling to the smallest tier that still meets quality needs when issuing many calls back to back, since larger tiers raise timeout_ms substantially and reduce how many concurrent requests the local machine can serve.

ecosystem and packageName must both be set and spelled exactly as the registry lists them; a name that only exists under a different ecosystem than the one given returns zero advisories rather than searching across ecosystems.
Must be the project's identifier or slug as returned by an earlier list or search call, not the display name shown in the interface, since free-text names are not accepted here.

REQUIRES the Desktop Bridge plugin already running and connected; calling this while the plugin is closed times out rather than queuing the rename, so check the connection first if an earlier call this session failed.
Run createCollection first if the collection does not exist yet; an id that was never created fails the whole batch rather than creating the collection implicitly on the fly.

Must match the organization that actually owns both appName and the change request sn; supplying an organizationId from a different organization returns not-found rather than cancelling a request that exists elsewhere.

Call list_models first to confirm which model values are currently accepted; an unsupported model string fails the call rather than falling back to a default. Set output_dir only when the result should be persisted to disk.

Call this before search_products or get_product so filters reference category slugs that actually exist in the BuyWhere catalog; passing an unrecognized slug elsewhere returns an empty result set rather than an error.
Use only in sandbox or demo workspaces; amount_usd must be a positive number, and calling check_balance afterward confirms the credit was applied before running cost estimates with estimate_cost.

Run this after parallel_init has created the project; if projectRoot is omitted the tool searches upward from the current directory, which can pick the wrong project when nested workspaces share a parent folder.
Run n8n_lint_workflow before activating a workflow for the first time; activating one with unresolved trigger errors silently fails to register the trigger instead of raising an exception.

Must be a single absolute URI beginning with http:, https:, file:, or data: -- relative paths and bare filenames are rejected, and a data: URI should include its media type so the converter picks the right parser.

Call list_sites first to obtain a valid siteUrl; date ranges longer than about 90 days should be split across multiple calls, since rowLimit caps each response and truncates rather than paginating automatically.

If the response is truncated at max_length, re-call with start_index set to the previous end to continue reading; for HTML pages prefer fetch_readable or fetch_markdown instead of parsing raw JSON here.
Provide a syntactically valid email address; if double opt-in is active for the list, the contact stays pending until they confirm, so a successful call is not proof the address is deliverable.

location_name is required and must follow the hierarchical, most-specific-first format described for that field; only set os once device is given, since accepted values differ between desktop and mobile.

Safe to call once per workspace; calling it again after the booking page already exists updates the configuration in place rather than duplicating it, and any field left out of config keeps its current value.

Call this first to confirm the connection to the server is alive before running statement_query or the contract export tools; a successful reply proves nothing about database credentials, only that the process is reachable.
Only call this after record_video has started a capture; calling it with no active recording is a harmless no-op, and the video file is not finalized on disk until this returns successfully.

The duration returned here is estimated from transcript timing, not the platform's own metadata; call get_youtube_transcript separately when you need exact caption timestamps instead of relying on this estimate.
1-indexed; requesting page 0 or a negative number returns the first page rather than an error, so check the response's own pagination metadata to know when you have reached the last page.
Default mode overwrite replaces the note's full content, so call read_note first if you need to preserve existing text, and prefer patch_note when you only want to change part of an existing note.
source must point to an existing vault directory the process can already read, not a URL; setting auto to true re-checks that path on an interval, so avoid pointing it at a slow network share.
Use this only to verify the server is reachable and echoing correctly; it performs no other work, so call help instead if you are looking for a list of what the other tools do.

Call mcp__getDsl first and take each URL only from its componentDocumentLinks array; fetch them one at a time in the order listed, since later documents can assume conventions defined in earlier ones.
app must be the exact application identifier, not a display name; call list_apps first if you are unsure of it, since an unrecognized name returns a not-found error rather than a search result.
Values can lag live exchange prints by up to a few minutes even though the tool name says real-time, so avoid polling this more than once a minute when watching intraday moves.

This iterates every tenant and every solution in one request, so it can take noticeably longer than a single-tenant lookup; run it for periodic audits rather than in a loop that checks one tenant at a time.

Both source_id and target_id must already exist as memory nodes before calling this; relation must be one of the six supported types exactly as spelled, since an unrecognized value creates an edge later traversal will silently skip.
Leave example empty first to see the exact list of valid names before requesting one by name; an unrecognized example value returns an empty result rather than the closest match.

period only accepts 7d or 30d, not an arbitrary range; raise min_shared above its default when the token universe is large, or the pair list fills with coincidental overlap rather than genuine coordination.

Prefer this over raw x/y coordinates whenever the element exposes an accessibility label or testID, since coordinate-based presses break as soon as the layout shifts between app versions or screen sizes.
Accepts any UTF-8 string, including empty; this tool only demonstrates round-tripping through the server and is not a substitute for add or debug when you need actual computation.

Call this before get-transcript to see which language codes actually exist for the video; requesting a caption language that is not in this list fails instead of falling back to auto-generated captions.
This must be the exact event identifier returned by a prior lookup, not a title guess; deletion is permanent and, unless sendUpdates is set to none, notifies every attendee immediately.

Runs inside the page's own JavaScript context, not Node, so it cannot reach the local filesystem; use puppeteer_navigate for page loads instead of triggering navigation from inside a script passed here.
packageId must match the pkg_ prefix format returned by fin_deepagent_packages; call that list tool first if you do not already have an id, since free-text package names are not accepted here.
Leave schematic empty first to see the full list of available names and their options before picking one; the name must match the CLI's own schematic name exactly, including case.

Call this before reset_session or close_session to confirm the session_id is still valid rather than reusing one from memory, since sessions past session_timeout auto-close and stop accepting that session_id entirely.

Call outline first if you do not already know the exact heading, top-level key, or row range to request; heading matching is case-insensitive but otherwise exact, so a reworded heading returns nothing.
Only SELECT statements are accepted; sql containing INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE, or DDL keywords is rejected by the server before execution, so there is no need to add a LIMIT purely to avoid write risk.

Omit body unless pricing is dynamic; probing with a sample body can hit the origin's own rate limits over repeated calls, so cache the schema for an endpoint rather than re-checking it before every fetch.

instance_id must be an existing cache instance's UUID, not a project name; call brain_stats first if you are unsure which instance is active, since an unrecognized UUID returns an empty list rather than an error.

languageId must match one of the server's supported identifiers exactly, such as the runtime name in lowercase; code runs in an isolated, time-limited sandbox, so long-running or interactive snippets are terminated before they finish.
parentId must be a folder ID already visible to list_files or get_file, not a path string; for large binary uploads use a dedicated upload flow rather than passing content inline here.

domain should be the bare registrable domain, not a full URL or an individual email address; supplying first_name and last_name narrows results to one person rather than every address indexed for that domain.

Must match the exact lowercase name returned by list_shadcn_components, such as its kebab-case identifier rather than the capitalized display name shown in the docs; an unrecognized name returns no examples, not a fuzzy match.

id must be the numeric card identifier such as 145789, not the card's title; call get_card_current_status first to confirm you have the right card, since a posted comment cannot be recalled once sent.

segmentId should come from explore-segments rather than guessed, since an invalid id fails instead of matching a similarly named segment; set starred to false to unstar, this single call handles both directions.

Must be a valid arXiv category code like cs.AI, not a free-text subject name; call list_categories first when unsure of the exact code, since a misspelled one returns zero results, not the nearest match.

Must reference a challenge whose source_type is exactly rlm_trajectory; passing the id of a challenge with a different source type fails validation before a workspace is created, so confirm the type beforehand rather than guessing.

Call this once before create_new_diagram or edit_diagram; calling it again while a session is already open can bind a second local port and leave the first preview window out of sync with later edits.
currencies entries must be uppercase three-letter ISO 4217 codes; passing a lowercase or invalid code errors the whole request rather than silently dropping just that one currency from the result.

Each entry in documentSpecs needs either id or url, not necessarily both; batch every document you need into one call instead of looping this tool once per document, since each call carries its own overhead.
kind, when set, must be one of component, example, or style; any other value is ignored rather than rejected, and increasing offset by the previous limit pages past the default 25 results.
Case-sensitive and single-use; call auth first to confirm you are signed in to the right account, since redeeming this code against the wrong account cannot be undone or reassigned afterward.

jo, when provided, narrows the result to a single article by its official article number rather than a keyword; omit efYd to get the article as currently in force instead of its wording on a specific past date.

parent must include its resource-type prefix, such as projects/ or folders/, not the bare ID alone; pageToken must be copied verbatim from the previous response's nextPageToken, since a hand-edited token is rejected, not ignored.

Runs inside the named service's container, defaulting to laravel_app when service is omitted; avoid long-running or interactive processes here, since the call blocks until the command exits and output returns only at the end.
query matches on series text and titles, not the internal series ID; increase offset by your previous limit to page through more results rather than requesting a very large limit in one call.

Every operation's path must be the literal string /users; batch every add and remove for a team into the same operations array so they apply atomically, since separate calls can interleave with another admin's concurrent patch.

Provide a specific phrase rather than a single word, since a broad topic like history produces generic, unfocused slides; generation can take up to a minute, so avoid retrying before the first call returns.
Pairs with connect-to-editor; skipping this call after you finish leaves your presence indicator visible to other collaborators in the dashboard until the connection times out on its own.

datetime must include an explicit UTC offset, not a bare local time, since an ambiguous timestamp shifts the calculated chart by hours; target_year narrows the search window rather than guaranteeing an opposition that exact year.

Leave methodology on auto unless a specific framework such as scamper is explicitly required, since the default already picks a fitting one; pushing ideaCount much above twenty tends to lower the quality of the later ideas.

Call this after onesub_simulate_purchase or onesub_simulate_webhook, pointing serverUrl at the same instance those calls used, since checking a different server returns an empty state that looks like the purchase never happened.

identifier must match a supported WildFly version or feature pack exactly as published, not a partial version; if you already know the resource address, call describe_resource directly instead of searching for its operations by keyword.

Provide either command with server_args for a local stdio server, or server_url for a remote one, not both; save the returned session_id immediately, since inspector_call_tool and the other inspector tools require it on every call.
Requires an exact, case-sensitive class name with no wildcard support; use namePattern instead when you only have a partial name or want to match several classes with * or ? in one call.

device must be an identifier returned by mobile_list_available_devices, not a display name typed from memory; if saveTo already exists it is overwritten silently, so use a unique filename per capture in a sequence of screenshots.

Must be the cluster's full https URL, not a bare cluster name or short alias; pair it with a database that actually exists on that cluster, since a mismatched pair returns zero tables rather than an error.

projectPath must be the group/project path, not a numeric ID, and iid is the merge request's number within that project, not a global ID. Leave userCredentials unset unless you must query as a different user than the configured token.

Each element needs numeric x and y values; set a matching group string only when points should be colored and split into a legend by category. A single point renders but shows no relationship, so include several.
Matches the keyword against article titles first and body text second, ignoring accent marks and letter case during comparison.
Returned metadata includes the module's most recently published version, its complete input and output variable lists, and an array of upstream dependency names.
Each entry in the response reports cluster name, current status, node count, and control-plane version, grouped under the location that was queried.
Once posted, the response body carries the new comment's identifier, author handle, and creation timestamp, with markdown left unrendered in the returned text.
What comes back mirrors the server's raw JSON payload, including any partial data alongside an errors array when part of the query fails.
This field expects a path to a JSON configuration file, either relative or absolute; a missing file yields an empty context block rather than an error.
The report lists a numeric score between 0 and 100 plus a list of flagged issues, each tagged with a category and a short remediation note.
On success, the response reports the order's final status, the quantity filled before cancellation, and an exchange-assigned timestamp marking when cancellation was recorded.
Guides are delivered as plain text with section headings, covering topics such as installation paths, theme extension, and plugin registration order.
Plain brand-style words or short phrases are expected here, without a top-level domain suffix; internal spaces are converted to hyphens before variation generation runs.
The response payload holds a boolean success flag and, on failure, a short diagnostic string identifying which precondition was not satisfied.
Output arrives as plain text sized for direct inclusion in a conversation, organized into headings and short examples grouped by topic.
A null result means no matching channel exists yet rather than one being created, while a found match includes the channel's creation date.
The response holds the full color palette, radius tokens, and font family settings stored for that theme, serialized as a flat key-value object.
Listings run from the most recent filing to the oldest, with filing date, form type, and a link to the filed document text included for each.
Each item in the returned array keeps the original URL alongside the extracted content and a status field noting whether that particular fetch succeeded.
Duration is expressed in seconds as a floating point value, resolution as width by height in pixels, and codec as its short identifying name.
Events arrive in chronological order, with start time, end time, and calendar name attached to each entry that falls within the requested range.
The value stored here is an opaque alphanumeric string of variable length, kept in local configuration and shown masked in later status responses.
Executions are listed oldest first within the requested window, with each record showing the run identifier, the triggering branch name, and the action's outcome.
This parameter takes a fully qualified filesystem path starting at the root; a leading tilde or relative dot segment is not expanded automatically.
The created annotation's numeric ID appears in the response along with the resolved start and end timestamps, expressed in epoch milliseconds throughout.
A standard 36-character UUID with hyphens identifies the snapshot here; matching against stored records is case-insensitive.
The connection URI supplied here combines host, port, and database name together, while the credential segment is kept out of logs and omitted from responses.
This field holds the alphanumeric agent identifier assigned during account setup, matched against the record created when the wallet was first linked.
Each lesson's completion state is reported as a boolean, alongside a single percentage figure summarizing overall progress through the course material.
The assembled context arrives as plain text sized for direct reuse, with earlier sections separated by simple headings rather than nested formatting.
Each cluster in the response contains a short label, a list of contributing paper titles, and a paragraph summarizing the theme shared across them.
Values here fall between 0 and 1 as a decimal figure; higher numbers narrow the results toward closer content matches by similarity score.
The response lists each retried connection's name alongside its new status, reporting either success or the specific error returned by that attempt.
Run as a preview, the response marks each step as simulated and leaves out any side-effect results that a live execution would otherwise include.
Pagination here counts the offset in whole records rather than bytes, and the limit field caps how many records a single call returns.
A fully qualified address beginning with the http or https scheme belongs here; addresses lacking an explicit scheme are rejected before the page loads.
Rows are returned as an array of objects keyed by column name, with numeric and date columns preserving their original database types.
Each audit entry lists an operation type, a timestamp, and a short description of what changed, ordered from most recent to oldest.
Source is returned as plain text in the project's existing formatting style, including inline comments and import statements exactly as stored.
The returned signature reports parameter names, inferred types, and the symbol's documentation comment when the source file provides one.
Each listed file shows its ingestion status as a boolean, while externally ingested items appear in a separate section below the file list.
Score fields range from 0 to 100, and the risk rating comes back as a short text label rather than a numeric value.
Confirmation arrives as a boolean success flag alongside the emoji identifier that was removed, without additional message metadata attached.
Saved exports use a plain text transcript format with one message per line, and timestamps are expressed in the export's local time zone.
Document references form an array of objects, each listing a document type label, a file name, and an issued date when available.
Search results are paginated at a fixed page size and ranked by relevance to the supplied query text, with the closest matches listed first.
Steps are presented as a numbered list matching a typical fresh project setup, with framework-specific package names substituted automatically based on the selected value.
Return values are serialized to JSON when possible, while non-serializable results such as DOM elements are converted to a short text summary instead.
Each result shows a star rating out of five, the total review count, and a formatted address string with the postal code included.
Vertex counts in the output typically fall well below the input total, while overall bounding-box dimensions remain unchanged after simplification runs.
Progress streams as a sequence of status lines showing layer download percentage, continuing until the local copy matches the registry's manifest digest.
Column names in the result set match the query's select list exactly, including any aliases, while row order follows underlying storage unless sorted explicitly.
The combined report merges every section's fields into one object, with a top-level summary score computed from the underlying checks.
Each deployment record shows a build duration in seconds and a status string such as success, failed, or in progress, alongside its identifier.
This path points to an existing container instance under which the new hierarchy attaches, with segments separated by forward slashes.
The returned object reflects the service's current traffic split across revisions, expressed as a percentage that sums to one hundred across all listed revisions.
The returned value is JSON-serialized when the expression resolves to a plain object, array, string, number, or boolean, and left empty otherwise.
Output duration generally runs a few seconds, with resolution matching the source image's aspect ratio and the file returned in a common video container format.
The internal identifier issued when the account was first connected goes here, distinct from the handle or display name shown to viewers.
Confirmation of deletion names the removed inbox's identifier; the messages that inbox previously contained are not part of the response.
The version action returns a plain semantic version string, while the info action returns a structured object with the project's display name and icon path.
Matching runs against visible rendered text rather than underlying HTML attributes, and the first matching element found is the one hovered.
A positive integer here bounds how many messages appear in a single page of the response; omitting it returns every message in one batch.
